_provenance_rule: Every value here traces to a published paper figure/table. No value in this file may come from running this repository's own stack (that would be a pinning run, which the parity goldens already cover).

ioi.clean_logit_diff.paper: Wang et al. 2023, Interpretability in the Wild (IOI), arXiv:2211.00593
ioi.clean_logit_diff.metric: mean logit(IO) - logit(S) at the END position over the clean IOI distribution

source.where: paper section 3 (metric F baseline, computed on 100,000 examples)
source.quote: GPT-2 small has a mean logit difference of 3.56

ioi.clean_logit_diff.notes: The paper's 3.56 is a 100k-example mean; this test pins N=512 seeded prompts, and the +/-1.2 band absorbs the smaller sample. Query-side path patching and attention-pattern checks are out of scope in protocol v1 (no pre-RoPE per-head query; attention_probs unsupported by the reference backend).

ioi.io_over_s_rate.paper: Wang et al. 2023, Interpretability in the Wild (IOI), arXiv:2211.00593
ioi.io_over_s_rate.metric: fraction of clean IOI prompts where logit(IO) > logit(S)

source.quote: IO predicted over S 99.3% of the time

ioi.io_over_s_rate.notes: Secondary assert. Floor set generously below the paper's 99.3% for the small-N regime.

rome.ate.paper: Meng et al. 2022, Locating and Editing Factual Associations in GPT (ROME), arXiv:2202.05262
rome.ate.metric: average total effect: mean over facts of P_clean(object) - P_corrupted(object), corruption = Gaussian noise (3*sigma of the embedding matrix) on subject-token embeddings

source.quote: The ATE of this experiment is 18.6%

rome.ate.notes: Facts are the paper's own tracing set (known_1000.json, 1209 facts, sha256-pinned in gen_counterfact.py), split into equal-subject-width documents (w2-w5) and pooled by the test - an earlier CounterFact-tracing sample measured ATE ~36 (regime mismatch: easier facts; clean baseline 0.38 vs the paper's 0.27), while known_1000 reproduces the clean baseline almost exactly (measured 0.2649). The correctness filter stays loose because easy facts raise the clean baseline and move the ATE with it. Known residual deviation: our seeded gaussian corrupts harder than the paper's (corrupted 0.031 vs 0.0847 at the same 3*sigma = 0.1447), pushing the ATE toward the band's upper half. Noise std is 3*sigma of the embedding matrix, not sqrt(3*sigma). MPS pre-verification: 23.35.

rome.hidden_aie_peak.metric: peak average indirect effect of single-layer hidden-state restoration at the last subject token, over the layer sweep

source.quote: AIE = 8.7% at layer 15, at the last subject token

rome.hidden_aie_peak.notes: Not a headline paper number; band width +/-4 mirrors the tolerance used for the MLP AIE peak. Peak layer is asserted loosely (early-to-middle third of the 48 layers).

rome.mlp_window_aie_peak.metric: peak average indirect effect of 10-layer-window MLP restoration ([l-4, l+5], clipped at edges) at the last subject token
rome.mlp_window_aie_peak.notes: The 10-layer window needs 10 simultaneous swap sites per point, which one sweep axis cannot express - the test generates one document per window programmatically (the parity-goldens build-doc-per-case pattern).

mixing.positional_share_edges.paper: Mixing Mechanisms: How Language Models Retrieve Bound Entities In-Context, arXiv:2510.06182
mixing.positional_share_edges.metric: share of queries attributed to the positional mechanism at FIRST and LAST group positions, at the most-mixed layer (~18)

source.where: paper Fig 2 (value read off the figure, not stated in text)
source.quote: A U-shaped curve emerges: first and last indices rely more on the positional mechanism

mixing.positional_share_edges.notes: The 80% center is figure-eyeballed (the paper text is only qualitative), hence confidence: low; a [60, 100] band would exceed the metric's range at the top, so the intent is one-sided and is encoded as a floor at 60. Attribution is candidate-relative (each mechanism's predicted genre vs the original answer, largest positive logit shift wins) at layer 18, the paper's own intervention layer for gemma-2-2b-it - past retrieval (L20+) the patch carries the counterfactual's finished answer and reflexive sweeps to ~100%. H100 corroboration (one run of test_mixing_positional_shares): pooled edges ~78% at L18 (first 90%, last 65%), tracking the figure-read 80%.

mixing.positional_share_middle.metric: share of queries attributed to the positional mechanism at MIDDLE group positions, at the most-mixed layer (~18)

source.quote: In middle entity groups, however, its effect becomes minimal, accounting only for 20% of the model's behavior

mixing.positional_share_middle.notes: The paper pins no dataset size; this test pins its own seeded N (150 rows per position bucket). Candidate-relative attribution at layer 18 (see the edges entry). H100 corroboration (one run of test_mixing_positional_shares): middle 17% at L18, tracking the paper's stated 20%.

arithmetic.hours_baseline_acc.paper: Arithmetic in the Wild: Llama uses Base-10 Addition to Reason About Cyclic Concepts, arXiv:2605.01148
arithmetic.hours_baseline_acc.metric: no-intervention accuracy on all 1,152 hours prompts (24 concepts x 48 spelled-out offsets, exact paper template)
arithmetic.hours_baseline_acc.notes: match is exact next-token equality on a single-token column. Tokenization rule (Llama-3.1 never merges space+digits, but bare zero-padded hours are single tokens): the prompt carries the trailing space ('... it will be ') and the answer column is the bare zero-padded hour, asserted single-token by the fixture generator. Any consistent, stated tokenization rule is acceptable.

arithmetic.steering_top1_fraction.metric: fraction of the 24 steering targets whose target hour token is top-1 in the prompt-averaged post-steering distribution (layer 18 residual, last token, alpha=10, periods {2,5,10,20,50}, prompts filtered to baseline-correct only)

source.where: paper Fig 7 diagonal, operationalized by the task author (a co-first-author of the paper)
source.quote: require that the fraction of the 24 steering targets whose target token receives the highest prompt-averaged probability is at least 0.8 (i.e., >= 20 of 24 targets)

arithmetic.steering_top1_fraction.notes: The paper's figure reads as 0.85 +/- 0.1 and the criterion is one-sided ('a higher fraction is better, never worse'), so a floor at 0.8 is used. Anti-gaming constraints are enforced in code: all 24 targets steered, fixed period set, prompt filter is baseline correctness only. Top-1 is taken over the 24 hour tokens' prompt-averaged probabilities (the diagonal's own support); the per-prompt Eq. 4 correction runs as a local-only pytorch_fn edit in generated documents, with the pinned harvest document feeding the test-side probe fit.
